interconnection_url.notes: South Dakota does not require or offer full retail-rate net metering. The South Dakota Public Utilities Commission's own Solar Energy FAQ page states directly: 'South Dakota does not compensate solar generation at a net metered rate.' Instead, Xcel Energy's own PUC-filed South Dakota Electric Rate Book, Section 9, governs Small Qualifying Facility (SQF) interconnection and compensation under Rate Code E50.

value.program_or_pathway: Small Qualifying Facility (SQF) interconnection under Xcel Energy's (Northern States Power Company) South Dakota Electric Rate Book, Section 9. South Dakota does not offer net metering; excess generation delivered to Xcel Energy is instead compensated under Rate Code E50 (Occasional Delivery Energy Service).
other_conditions: The South Dakota Public Utilities Commission's own Solar Energy FAQ states directly that South Dakota does not compensate solar generation at a net-metered rate.
Compensation for energy delivered to Xcel Energy under Rate Code E50 is capped at a maximum of 2,000 kWh per month; any energy delivered above this monthly cap is uncompensated.
The minimum contracted term of service under the SQF tariff is 12 months.
The SQF must install a Xcel Energy-approved, lockable disconnect switch located near the interconnection point, with unrestricted utility access at all times.
The SQF owner must maintain liability insurance of at least $300,000 per occurrence for the duration of the agreement.

No specific interconnection system-size (kW) cap was found in the tariff sections fetched this session; the tariff instead defines eligibility by 'Small Qualifying Facility' status without stating a numeric kW ceiling in the sections reviewed.
